attributes.body_ja:
「ばこそ」は、「からこそ」と同（おな）じように使（つか）われる文法（ぶんぽう）で、(A) が (B) の正確（せいかく）な理由（りゆう）や原因（げんいん）であることを表（あらわ）します。意味（いみ）は「まさに (A) だから」や「(A) の場合（ばあい）だけ (B) だ」です。これは、接続助詞（せつぞくじょし）「ば」と、副助詞（ふくじょし）「こそ」の組（く）み合（あ）わせです。

「ばこそ」は仮定形（かていけい）であれば、ほとんどすべての語句（ごく）の後（あと）に置（お）くことができます。ただし、名詞（めいし）やナ形容詞（けいようし）の後（あと）では、「であればこそ」という形（かたち）を使（つか）いましょう。

(A) には、一見（いっけん）すると (B) の理由（りゆう）とは思（おも）えないような内容（ないよう）が来（く）ることがよくあります。そのため、話（はな）し手（て）は「こそ」を使（つか）って、(A) が (B) の理由（りゆう）であることをはっきりと示（しめ）そうとします。

注意点（ちゅういてん）

「ばこそ」は非常（ひじょう）に硬（かた）く、少（すこ）し古風（こふう）な表現（ひょうげん）です。現代（げんだい）では、一般的（いっぱんてき）に「からこそ」が使（つか）われます。
attributes.body:
ばこそ is used in a similar way to からこそ, indicating that (A) is the precise reason for (B). It will be translated as 'precisely because of (A)', or 'it is only due to (A) that (B)'. This pattern is a combination of the conjunction particle ば, and the adverbial particle こそ, which is being used in a similar way to a sentence ending particle in this case.

ばこそ may follow almost any word type that has been adjusted into its hypothetical form. However, it will appear as であればこそ when used after nouns or な-Adjectives.

In many cases, (A) will be a reason that is difficult to conceive of as what would lead to (B) under normal circumstances, and therefore requires the speaker to emphasize it with こそ.

Caution

ばこそ is very formal, and a bit old-fashioned, so からこそ will almost always be the preferred choice in modern day Japanese.

attributes.source: A Dictionary of Advanced Japanese Grammar

attributes.body: Both use the emphatic こそ but differ by verb form. ～ばこそ is conditional, meaning only if (A), then (B), as in 忙しければこそ 'precisely because you're busy'. ～てこそ focuses on completion, meaning only after (A) happens, then (B), as in 苦労してこそ成功がある ('Only after hardship comes success'). ～ばこそ can introduce a hypothetical condition, while ～てこそ emphasizes the actual realization of (A).

attributes.body: Despite appearing different, ～ばこそ and からこそ are essentially synonymous in meaning, both expressing an reason for something, i.e. 'it is precisely because of (A) that (B)'. The main difference is that ～ばこそ is a highly formal and literary expression found primarily in writing, while からこそ is far more common and used in everyday speech as well as writing.
